hook: Argue a case in written German, and find out whether it holds together.
intro: A Stellungnahme has four parts: a position, reasons for it, an honest look at the other side, and a conclusion. Write 600 to 1300 characters. The part most people skip is the objection, and it is the part that earns the marks: naming the strongest thing the other side says, and answering it, is what separates an argument from an opinion. Watch your connectors too. Each one claims a relation between two sentences, and the correction will check whether that relation is really there.
tips[0].title: Position first, not last
tips[0].text: German argumentative writing puts the thesis at the top. The reader should know where you stand by the second sentence; everything after that is support. Saving it for the end reads as indecision.
tips[0].check.why: The thesis goes first; the rest of the text supports it.
tips[1].title: Concede, then answer
tips[1].text: An objection you name yourself is worth more than two more arguments of your own. State it in the other side’s words with zwar, gewiss or sicherlich, then turn it with allerdings, dennoch or jedoch. Turning it is the step people forget.
tips[1].check.why: zwar sets up a concession and needs a turn; außerdem would simply add.
tips[1].trap: A concession with no turn reads as agreement with the other side.
tips[1].visual.rows[0].b: doch langfristig spart die Stadt Geld.
tips[2].title: Every connector is a claim
tips[2].text: folglich claims a consequence, zudem claims another point of the same kind, dennoch claims a contrast that survives. Put the wrong one in and the argument reads as broken even though every sentence is correct.
tips[2].check.why: Moving away is the consequence of the rents, not a contrast with them.
remember[0]: Thesis in the first two sentences, then the support.
remember[1]: Two arguments, each with a reason and an example or a figure.
remember[2]: Zwar …, allerdings …: concede, then turn. The turn is the point.
remember[3]: Every connector claims a relation; make sure it is the real one.
exam: A written Stellungnahme is the core writing task of the B2 certificate, and the shape of every opinion piece in a German newspaper.
mistakes[0].why: zwar demands a turn, not another point on the same side.
mistakes[1].why: A reason has to add something the claim did not already say.
mistakes[2].why: No comma after the opening phrase; the verb follows it directly.
mistakes[3].why: The conclusion has to follow from the argument you made.
tips[0].check.q: Where does the position belong in a Stellungnahme?
